medicinal_uses: Used historically as a stimulant and tonic (extremely dangerous).
cure_precaution: Requires emergency medical attention; often fatal without rapid treatment.

toxicity: Generally considered non-toxic, though some people may experience mild GI upset.
soil_preference: Well-drained, moderately fertile soil.
medicinal_uses: Sometimes used in traditional remedies for cough.
cure_precaution: Minimal risk; supportive care if needed.

toxicity: Seeds contain β-aminopropionitrile; ingestion over time can lead to lathyrism (muscle paralysis).
soil_preference: Fertile, well-drained soils with full sun.
medicinal_uses: None.
cure_precaution: Avoid eating seeds; seek medical attention if symptoms arise.

toxicity: Contains thujone; can cause convulsions, vomiting, and liver damage in large doses.
soil_preference: Well-drained, sandy or loamy soils.
medicinal_uses: Used historically for worm infestations and menstrual issues.
cure_precaution: Do not ingest; medical supervision required for poisoning.

toxicity: All parts are toxic; contains nicotine and anabasine alkaloids.
soil_preference: Dry, sandy soils; drought-resistant.
medicinal_uses: Used traditionally for respiratory and skin ailments (risky).
cure_precaution: Emergency care needed for ingestion or significant exposure.

toxicity: Berries contain oxalates; can cause nausea, vomiting, and kidney damage.
soil_preference: Well-drained, average soil in sun or shade.
medicinal_uses: Used in folk medicine for swelling and inflammation.
cure_precaution: Avoid ingestion; rinse mouth and seek care if symptoms arise.

toxicity: Extremely toxic; contains cicutoxin which causes seizures and death.
soil_preference: Wet soils near streams, ditches, and marshes.
medicinal_uses: None due to high toxicity.
cure_precaution: Seek emergency treatment immediately; often fatal.

toxicity: Contains tremetol; causes 'milk sickness' if livestock eat it.
soil_preference: Woodland edges; prefers moist, well-drained soil.
medicinal_uses: Historically used for fever and diarrhea (risky).
cure_precaution: Avoid ingestion; remove from grazing areas.

toxicity: Leaves and seeds contain cyanogenic glycosides; toxic when wilted.
soil_preference: Moist, fertile soils in forests and fields.
medicinal_uses: Used in cough syrups (bark only).
cure_precaution: Avoid wilted leaves; seek medical care for symptoms.

toxicity: Sap causes severe burns when exposed to sunlight (phytophotodermatitis).
soil_preference: Open, sunny areas with well-drained soil.
medicinal_uses: Historically used as a food crop; medicinal use not recommended.
cure_precaution: Wash skin immediately after contact; avoid sun exposure.

toxicity: Seeds and pods contain lectins; can cause nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.
soil_preference: Well-drained, fertile soils; prefers full sun.
medicinal_uses: No recognized medicinal uses.
cure_precaution: Avoid ingestion; supportive care for GI symptoms.

toxicity: Leaves contain oxalates; large quantities may cause kidney issues.
soil_preference: Disturbed, nutrient-rich soils.
medicinal_uses: Used for liver and skin conditions in herbal medicine.
cure_precaution: Avoid excess use; hydrate and monitor symptoms.

toxicity: Highly toxic; contains thevetin and peruvoside, cardiac glycosides.
soil_preference: Tropical, well-drained soils.
medicinal_uses: Used in traditional medicine (dangerous and discouraged).
cure_precaution: Immediate emergency treatment required; potentially fatal.

toxicity: Extremely toxic; all parts except the red aril contain taxine alkaloids which affect the heart and central nervous system.
soil_preference: Moist, well-drained soil; grows in both sun and shade.
medical_uses: Source of paclitaxel (Taxol), a chemotherapy drug used to treat various cancers.
properties: Cardiotoxic alkaloids (taxine A and B), anti-cancer compounds (paclitaxel).
cure_precaution: Ingestion requires immediate emergency treatment; no known antidote, supportive care and cardiac monitoring essential.
